messages:
anya: FYI nightly eval flagged a regression on the `legal-summaries` prompt set — lots of intermittent hallucinations and BLEU/ROUGE variance. looks like outputs differ run-to-run even with same model+seed :eyes:
ci-bot: nightly-eval: job/1975001229 finished; failures=12; top-failure=hallucination_rate_up (dashboard: https://dash.redwood/test/1975001229)
mike: can you paste the eval config + how you repro locally?
anya: repro steps below. quick note: this only shows up with prefix_cache enabled AND quantized q4_0 variant. disabling prefix cache removes nondet.

```bash
# run nightly eval locally (repro)
python eval/run_eval.py \
  --model rwd-3b-q4_0 \
  --promptset legal-summaries \
  --batch_size 2 \
  --prefix_cache true \
  --continuous_batching true \
  --seed 42 \
  --num_samples 200
```

anya: also tried with batch_size=1 (no regressions), batch_size=4 (sporadic). seems to be narrow window around small batch sizes.
sophia: curious — do you have cache key / slot logs for the diverging requests? could be shard/slot aliasing across tenants or prefix lengths.
anya: dumping a few lines from runtime debug:

```
[2026-03-19T03:12:10Z] tenant=redwood-prod req_id=abc123 pref_key=sha1:7c9d slot=17 prefix_len=64 seq=0
[2026-03-19T03:12:10Z] tenant=redwood-prod req_id=def456 pref_key=sha1:7c9d slot=17 prefix_len=64 seq=0
[2026-03-19T03:12:11Z] tenant=redwood-prod req_id=ghi789 pref_key=sha1:9a1b slot=5  prefix_len=32 seq=0
```

anya: note identical pref_key hash for different request ids. i think collisions happening when prefix normalization truncates to fixed window. :bug:
mike: so two different prefixes hashed to same slot/sha1? that'd explain cache poisoning between concurrent batches. do we know the hashing function/namespace salt used for pref_key?
anya: runtime currently uses murmur3_32(pref_string) + mod num_slots, no namespace salt for promptset-level.
david: could quantization change tokenization boundaries for prefixes (e.g., false boundaries when using packed batches) causing same normalized prefix string? or is it purely key-space collision?
luis: try running with `--cache_namespace=eval-legal-v2` to force a different salt and see if regression disappears. if so, we can short-term mitigate by namespacing nightly evals and push a fix for key derivation.
anya: ran that: added `--cache_namespace=eval-legal-v2` and reran 3x. regression gone in all runs.

mike: that strongly suggests collision/aliasing. long-term we should: 1) move to 64-bit hash + tenant+promptset salt, 2) bake prefix length into key, 3) make eviction deterministic across quant variants.
sophia: agree. also we should add a unit test that generates near-colliding prefixes (small edit distance) to exercise hash distribution.
david: also add an E2E perf test toggling continuous_batching on/off to catch this during model bring-up.
anya: created a quick repro harness: `tools/cache_repro/generate_collisions.py` — it brute-forces prefixes and reports slot collisions. i'll put PR with initial test.

```py
# snippet from generate_collisions.py
for a in prefixes:
  for b in prefixes:
    if a != b and hash(a) % SLOTS == hash(b) % SLOTS:
      print(f"collision: slot={hash(a)%SLOTS} a={a[:32]} b={b[:32]}")
```

luis: for immediate mitigation in prod nightly runs we should enable `cache_namespace` per-eval and set `max_batch_size >= 8` for evals, as smaller batch sizes are more likely to trigger these collisions due to packing heuristics.
mike: add a release blocker? feels risky to leave as-is for new quantized variants.
sophia: not a blocker if we can roll a hotfix that includes namespace salt + stronger hash; patch ETA?
anya: i'll open PR with unit test + runtime change to include tenant+promptset salt in key derivation. aiming for review today. owner: @anya.
david: i'll file an infra task to update nightly eval configs to set cache_namespace until fix is live. owner: @david.
mike: nice catch. please add to changelog and to model-onboarding checklist: "verify prefix cache no collisions for quantized variants". :white_check_mark:
anya: will do. closing loop after PR lands. thanks team! :tada:
